findings.note: front : back reads the same as back : front — an axis has two ends, not a start

notes:
set-directional's two pairs read as symmetric/reversible (order-indistinguishable), violating the axis relationship's requirement that the pair not be reversible without changing the claim; needs new word pairs, not just relabeling.
- set-directional: Both pairs (hearthstone:rooftop, windward:leeward) name two ends of a symmetric axis with no inherent start, so A:B reads identically to B:A — the relationship's own failure mode ('front:back reads the same as back:front') is triggered.
  Try: Replace both pairs with axis-pairs that have a non-arbitrary, inferable direction, e.g. 'foundation : chimney-cap' (base-to-top order implied by construction sequence) paired with another structure's base-to-top pair like 'keel : mast'
  Or: Reframe the set around a directional process instead of a static axis, e.g. 'spark : ember' and 'ember : ash' style cause-to-effect ordering (pick pairs where the first member necessarily precedes the second)
  Or: If a symmetric axis must be kept, change the relationshipLabel to explicitly state the pair is unordered ('two ends of one axis, order-free') and ensure the board format allows unordered sets — otherwise pair-author must supply ordered replacements
Do not change: set-object-component, set-taxonomic, set-sign-significant — no allowlisted finding touches them.
